parsed.explanation: The sharpest exposure is at the border: national guidance directs refusal where documents cast doubt on an applicant's sex, and suspected misrepresentation can support a lifetime fraud finding; at least eight governments have issued advisories and some foreign nationals were detained over visa issues. Below that, the division documents birth-sex custody placement with a male-guard search despite a female licence marker, a severe municipal restroom ordinance, and an August 2026 mob beating after which the trans victims — not the attackers — were charged; one was denied hospital care and jailed with men. There is no state gender-identity anti-discrimination or hate-crime coverage. No criminalisation of trans identity and no statewide facilities statute, so severity stays below imprisonment-as-standard jurisdictions.

entry_documents.exposure: National cable: refuse where documents/records cast doubt on sex; suspected wilful misrepresentation may support permanent lifetime ineligibility under the fraud ground; trans-athlete entry ban; some foreign nationals detained; eight governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented for trans visitors; marker litigation unresolved and does not restrain screening.
entry_documents.interaction: Border refusal strands the traveller and can bar future travel; no downstream facility or custody safeguard follows.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Trans woman held in a men's facility and searched by a male guard despite a female licence marker (Aug 2026); immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse of trans men; corrections policies removing hormones.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute only; state bias statute excludes gender identity.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any arrest or immigration hold routes to birth-sex custody regardless of documents.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: One municipality enacted one of the country's most severe anti-trans restroom ordinances; documented trespass arrest of a student held in a men's ward. Statewide facilities position not established.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No statewide facilities statute documented either way.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Local police enforce the municipal ordinance; state silence leaves the local rule operative.

care_services.exposure: A mob-attack victim was denied hospital care; minors' gender-affirming care banned since Jan 2024; transition care excluded from insurance and public coverage.
care_services.interaction: Emergency disclosure of trans status can precede denial; care bans are resident-facing but signal institutional posture.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National order directs investigation of schools and prosecution of teachers facilitating a minor's social transition; counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy states powers will not target mere disagreement; several orders enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: A travelling family with a trans minor entering school or clinical settings could trigger referral.

minors_guardians.exposure: State minors' care ban in force; national orders criminalising facilitation of social transition.
minors_guardians.interaction: Whether a visiting minor's existing prescription is honoured is unresolved.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Aug 2026 mob beating over restroom use; victims charged with disturbing the peace, no attacker arrested that day; highest reported per-capita trans killing rate (undercount floor, given no weight).
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute; state statute omits gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local charging discretion turned on the victims, showing absent street-level recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No state gender-identity anti-discrimination law; no gender-identity hate-crime coverage; state employment protections lapsed; plea outcome unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Two municipalities prohibit gender-identity discrimination; national employment ruling nominally applies but is contested.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse depends on municipality; elsewhere national processes are the only route.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar border-flagging and denial of entry, but there statutes barred detention and no further layers existed. Here refusal can carry a lifetime ineligibility finding, and the division adds documented birth-sex custody harm and violence with the victims charged, placing it below.

Far worse: there exposure reliably produced transfer to a maximum-security penitentiary with decades of hard labour as the standard outcome. Here no law criminalises trans identity or expression, so imprisonment is not the expected consequence of discovery.

There an advocate invoked a directive that actually worked and produced the prescription. Here no documented protection operates for a trans visitor at the border, in custody, or in local facilities, so the case sits below that tier.

parsed.synthesis: A traveller with consistent documents and no arrest may move through much of this jurisdiction without state action, and no law criminalises trans identity. But the operative regime fails at the points where disclosure is engineered: visa screening that can refuse and permanently bar, arrest or immigration hold that places by birth sex and searches by male guards, a municipal restroom ordinance, and local police who charged the victims of a mob beating. No working remedy is documented; municipal protections in two cities do not reach the visitor's itinerary.
